rationale:
bugs_open/097 has been open since 2026-07-26. Its repair half is done and live: RepairPageLinks now runs at four seams and removes dead internal links from the markup that ships. Its HEADLINE half is untouched, and the file states it in its own words: 'the repair now deletes a phantom link silently, and the authoring defect that wrote it goes unreported'.

The reason it goes unreported is structural, not an oversight. Every mechanism the platform has for 'does this button point at a real page' answers by ENUMERATING field names: ctaFieldNames covers 6 components x 2 named top-level fields, and DeriveCTAURLFields (the schema-derived successor staged on council trail 2525f980) covers top-level '<stem>_url' fields that have a label sibling. Neither can see a url that lives anywhere else, and anywhere else is where most of them live.

Measured against production on 2026-08-02 by RUNNING THE SHIPPING CODE over all 885 page_components.content_data rows (not a SQL approximation of it): 52 stored internal page links resolve to no page on their own site, across 7 domains, in 4 components - and NOT ONE of those 4 components is covered by either enumeration. 36 of the 52 sit at cards[N].link_url, nested inside an array, where a top-level walker cannot reach them at any precedence; 10 sit at case-studies-grid's cardN_link_url, which the schema derivation cannot pair because there is no cardN_link_label. Adding a component to a list fixes that component and the next one reopens the gap - which is the shape 097 was filed about, and which its own fix candidate 1 asks to be closed by resolving links by what they ARE rather than by where they are declared.

The third representation is the part nobody had covered. A page has three copies of its links: the deployed string, the stored rendered_html, and the content_data the platform RE-RENDERS FROM. rerender_page_sections rebuilds each section from content_data with no writer pass, so a dead href left there is regenerated on every re-render, repaired again on the way out, and never once reported. component_link_repair.go (committed today by the 136 lane) names this exact limit and routes it here: 'content_data. Same limit as 079's fix ... The deployed artefact stays covered by the outbound rerender seam (repairOutboundPageLinks, bugs_open/097).'

This change adds the content_data pass at the SAME persistence chokepoint as the markup pass, off the SAME page index, with the SAME shared classifier. It nominates a candidate by field NAME at any depth and judges it by VALUE with ClassifyLinkScope, which is why it needs no exclusion list: an image_url holds /images/x.jpg (LinkScopeAsset) and a docs_url holds https://... (LinkScopeExternal), so neither is ever considered without this code naming either of them. The production run confirms it: zero non-page fields were nominated across 885 components, and 872 of the 885 produce no finding at all.
submitter: bug-097 content_data link resolution (bugs_open/097 headline half)

plan.summary: bugs_open/097's remaining defect: the platform resolves a component's link fields against real pages only for an enumerated set of components and top-level field names, so 52 live internal links stored in page_components.content_data point at no page and nothing reports them. This adds one nesting-agnostic pass at the save chokepoint that resolves EVERY url-named field in content_data against the same page index the markup repair uses. Two arms, deliberately asymmetric: rewrite when the target page exists and the writer only omitted the extension (19 of the 52), report-only when no page exists at all (33 of the 52). The phantom arm does not blank the field, because blanking is the content_data analogue of link_repair.go's unlink arm and that arm is disputed in its own header by the editquality and render_guardian seats - widening a disputed repair from the rendered copy to the SOURCE OF TRUTH is not a scope fix's to do.

edits.rationale: The rule, in one place, with no component list and no field list. It walks maps and slices alike so nesting cannot hide a link; nominates a candidate by field NAME (IsURLFieldName - a shape test, deliberately generous because it only nominates); and judges by VALUE via the shared ClassifyLinkScope, which is what keeps image and off-site fields out without naming any of them. Rewrite emits a string the index handed back (a stored pages.url), never one assembled here - bugs_closed/029 was a whole bug about an emitter that assembled plausible URLs. Fail-open on an empty index, identically to RepairPageLinks: an empty index means 'the page set could not be read', never 'this site has no pages'.

The call shape and the durable record. It attaches the component name, because datahelpers reports a path inside one map and only this layer knows whose map it was - 'which component authors phantoms' is the question the record exists to answer. It exempts a runtime-fill section per section, in lockstep with the markup pass: its stored values are placeholders the client replaces, and skipping in lockstep is what stops content_data and rendered_html disagreeing about the same link until the next re-render. The record is a work RECORD not a work ITEM, on exactly the precedent writeLinkRepairLog set and for the reasons it states (bugs_open/083: nothing drains 'detected'; bugs_open/077: do not file items whose handler has no remit).

Runs the new pass off the index this function ALREADY loaded. Loading it twice would be two chances for the markup repair and the source-data audit to disagree about what a real page is, which is the divergence validate_page_content.go:272-277 already refuses between its own check and its own repair. Ordered before the markup repair so a rewritten source field and the anchor rendered from it are corrected in the same save rather than one save apart. The origin struct is hoisted so both records name the same path.

The bug in one test, plus the controls the design claims rest on. Every guard was proven load-bearing by MUTATION, not by assertion: dropping the value-scope guard makes 6 asset/external fields fire; dropping the empty-index fail-open makes a real link a phantom; stopping the array descent loses all 3 nested findings; making the phantom arm write to the map fails the source-is-untouched assertion; removing the path sort makes the order unstable within two runs. That last one found a real defect in my own first draft - a redundant key sort meant BOTH orderings could be deleted individually with every test still green, so neither was load-bearing. The redundant one was removed rather than kept as decoration.

The call-shape tests, each with the control that stops it passing vacuously. The runtime-fill test asserts the exemption AND then re-runs the identical section without the marker to prove it was the exemption doing the work rather than the absence of a link. The degrade test covers both routes to an untrusted index (indexOK=false with a populated index, and indexOK=true with an empty one) and asserts content_data was not mutated on either.

Detection and repair are not substitutes: the repair now deletes a phantom link silently, and the authoring defect that wrote it goes unreported.'

This catches the whole class regardless of which field or nesting the link came from, and it catches wrong-url as well as missing-page. Candidate 1 makes the bad state detectable wherever it appears; 2 and 3 both require someone to remember to extend a list, which is the shape that produced this bug.'

platform/orchestration/actions/component_link_repair.go (committed 2026-08-02 by the bugs_open/136 lane), WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER: 'content_data. Same limit as 079's fix: this repairs the STORED HTML, and a re-render from content_data can reintroduce the href in storage. The deployed artefact stays covered by the outbound rerender seam (repairOutboundPageLinks, bugs_open/097).'

platform/orchestration/datahelpers/ctafields.go header: the hand-maintained map 'covers 5 of the 33 component functions which actually declare CTA url fields'; and its derivation rule requires 'a sibling field of the SAME stem ... <stem>_label, <stem>_text, or the bare <stem>' - which case-studies-grid's cardN_link_url has none of.

LIVE input_schema of content_components.function='info-card-grid' (id fc56f085-8e9a-4f6b-8e8d-600f9a1381e2), read 2026-08-02: {"cards": {"type": "array", "source": "llm", "items": {"link_url": {"type": "url"}, "link_label": {"type": "text"}, ...}}} - the destination is inside the array items, so no top-level field walker reaches it.

Production run of the SHIPPING RepairContentDataLinks over all 885 page_components.content_data rows, 2026-08-02: components with findings 13; REWRITE (target page exists) 19; PHANTOM (no page row at all) 33; TOTAL 52. By component/arm: info-card-grid 21 phantom + 16 rewrite, case-studies-grid 10 phantom, tool-cta 3 rewrite + 1 phantom, platform-comparison 1 phantom. By domain: robot-hands.com 17, idea.uk 12, finetuning.uk 7, gaswholesalers.com 6, ai-agent-orchestration.com 5, leopardessconsulting.co.uk 4, vonc.com 1.

Fleet census of component schemas, 2026-08-02: 25 active component functions declare a URL field INSIDE an array's items (info-card-grid/hero-card-carousel/image-hover-card-grid/swipeable-insight-carousel cards[].link_url; tool-list/guide-list/game-list/news-listing/latest-news/directory-listing items[].url; filtered-result-grid results[].cta_url; and others). Every one of them is invisible to a top-level field walker.

Live pages rows proving the rewrite arm targets real pages, 2026-08-02: gaswholesalers.com has /contact.html (active, deployed) while its cards link /contact; idea.uk has /about.html, /report.html, /tools.html (all active, deployed) while its cards link /about, /report, /tools; robot-hands.com has /matchmatrix.html and /learning-center.html (active, deployed) while its cards link /matchmatrix and /learning-center - and /learning-center/index.html is 'archived', so it is correctly absent from the index the rewrite resolves against.

platform/orchestration/datahelpers/link_repair.go header, on the unlink arm this change declines to mirror: 'WHAT IS STILL OWED (deferred, not forgotten): decide whether unlink is the right repair action at all. If it is replaced by an escalation, this predicate should become element-scoped in the same change ... Raised by the council's editquality and render_guardian seats, round 1 of correlation 4465f655-c6c6-49b4-a9b8-4ca7a5f647df.'

platform/orchestration/actions/validate_page_content.go:272-277, the shared-index rule this change follows: 'The page set is loaded ONCE here and reused by the repair pass below, so detection and repair can never disagree about what a real page is.'
plan.risks:
1. THE REWRITE ARM MUTATES content_data, which is the source of truth. Measured, not argued: 19 of 885 components' worth of values change, all of them from a path that resolves to nothing to a stored pages.url on the same site, and every one is listed verbatim in the bug file. The semantics are RepairPageLinks' rewrite arm unchanged - same NormalizePagePath, same Lookup, same hrefSuffix - so a reviewer checking this is checking a live, already-reviewed rule applied to a second representation, not a new rule. 872 of 885 components are byte-identical after the pass.
2. THE PHANTOM ARM DOES NOT MUTATE, and a reviewer may reasonably ask why the fix stops short. The answer is in the plan summary and pinned by a test: blanking is the content_data analogue of a repair arm that link_repair.go's own header records as unsettled by two council seats. If the council rules the other way, the change is one branch and one test.
3. SCOPE. This covers the six agent types that persist body sections through SavePageSectionsAction. It is NOT fleet-wide coverage of page_components.content_data - the single-component writers listed in bugs_open/136 do not pass through here. That limit is stated in the file header rather than left to be inferred, and extending to them is the call shape component_link_repair.go already established, deliberately left as a separate change.
4. A THIRD agent_error_log code. CONTENT_DATA_LINK_AUDIT is new; CONTENT_LINK_REPAIR_DETAIL and CONTENT_LINK_REPAIR_SKIPPED are untouched, so every query already written against them returns exactly what it returned before. The reason for a new code rather than a shared one is the reason linkRepairErrorCode gives for being distinct from validationDetailErrorCode: it answers a different question - what the page's SOURCE still holds, versus what the gate changed in the markup that shipped.
5. NO MIGRATION, and that is deliberate. The 52 live findings clear as a side effect of ordinary operation: the next save of each page runs the pass, the 19 rewritable ones are corrected at source and the 33 phantoms are recorded. A reviewer should check they agree with that rather than with a one-off UPDATE over production content_data.
6. INTERACTION WITH THE STAGED CTA FLIP (council trail 2525f980, cta_link_integrity lane). This change does not touch ctaFieldNames, DeriveCTAURLFields, resolve_internal_links_action.go or rerender_page_sections_action.go, and does not alter the precedence the flip round will invert. It is complementary: the flip decides which fields a build-time resolver WRITES; this decides whether what was written, by anyone, at any depth, points at a real page. Named here so the flip round's reviewers are told rather than left to measure it.
